summary: systemd-udev rate-limit triggered by duplicate I2C/HID devices after BIOS update blocks depot provisioning
description:
Issue summary: Multiple depot-imaged laptops are failing to complete out-of-box provisioning after a vendor BIOS update. The provisioning agent stalls during first-boot user-profile creation; images do not reach final 'device enrolled' state.

Impact: Blocks re-deployed hardware from returning to users. ~12 devices across two weeks in the us-west depot. Causes delays to RMA turnarounds and increased manual triage.

Environment: Depot imaging pipeline (prod-us-west). Affected builds use corporate golden image (Windows 11 22H2 + corporate baseline) with vendor BIOS 1.43+ applied.

Observed behavior: On first boot, systemd logs show repeated rate-limited udev events for I2C/HID devices (appearing as duplicate entries) and a flood of udev triggers. systemd-udevd enforces rate limiting which delays device nodes creation, causing provisioning-agent services (profile-populate, smartcard-init hooks) to time out and the user profile creation to fail. Some devices reboot automatically and get into a provisioning loop.

Expected behavior: udev should enumerate I2C/HID devices once and provisioning completes within the normal time window (~6–8 minutes).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Apply vendor BIOS 1.43 or later to a Dell-Precision-5470 or Lenovo-ThinkPad-X13-Gen3
2) Flash corporate golden image via depot imaging agent and boot device in depot network (prod-us-west),
3) Observe first-boot systemd and provisioning logs; wait for user-profile creation step
4) Note udev event floods and provisioning-agent timeouts around user-profile hooks
logs: Oct 25 09:12:11 image-5470 kernel: input: HID 0bda:0166 as /devices/platform/i2c-adapter/i2c-0/0-0010/input/input7
Oct 25 09:12:11 image-5470 systemd-udevd[412]: rate limit hit, ignoring event (250 events/min limit)
Oct 25 09:12:15 provisioning-agent[2201]: hook 'populate-user-profile' timed out after 300s
comments: Lena Cho (2024-10-29): Raised after 3 devices failed in a single shift. Collected serials and BIOS versions. Escalating to infra on-call.
Marcus Reed (2024-10-30): Reproduced locally in depot lab VM with identical BIOS image. Captured udev logs. Suspect kernel/firmware changed PCI/I2C topology ordering.
SRE Team (2024-10-31): Correlated with Dell advisory about HID descriptor changes in BIOS 1.43. Filing a vendor request for details and a potential rollback image.
Firmware Eng (2024-11-01): Vendor provided microcode diff showing additional composite HID interfaces introduced for touchpad firmware; this matches duplicate device nodes observed.
Marcus Reed (2024-11-02): Implemented temporary workaround in provisioning-agent to increase udev listen windows and retry hooks on deferred device nodes. Testing in lab - looks promising.
Lena Cho (2024-11-02): Deployed hotspot with workaround to depot lab for extended soak. Will update SLA and manual triage instructions for depot techs.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Vendor BIOS change introduces additional composite HID endpoints which expose themselves as separate I2C HID devices. The kernel enumerates duplicates because descriptors changed, flooding udev. systemd-udevd's default ratelimit (250 events/min, 5s burst) triggers, causing device nodes to be delayed or dropped. Provisioning hooks assume device nodes appear within 120s; the udev delay causes timeouts.

Commands & artifacts: journalctl -k -b -u systemd-udevd produced repeated 'rate limit' entries. /sys/class/input shows multiple entries with identical names but different device IDs. Repro steps confirmed by re-flashing BIOS and toggling touchpad firmware mode. Captured kernel dmesg, vendor microcode changelog, and provisioning-agent debug logs attached.

Short-term workarounds validated: 1) Rolling back BIOS to 1.42 (manual vendor rollback) restores normal enumeration. 2) Increasing provisioning-agent device discovery timeout from 120s -> 600s prevents triage in most cases. 3) Add udev rule to coalesce duplicate I2C/HID devices by stable phys/path matching to avoid duplicate device nodes (requires careful testing).
resolution_notes:
Workaround deployed to depot lab (2024-11-02): provisioning-agent updated to retry device-dependent hooks up to 600s with exponential backoff (PR referenced above). Depot tech runbook updated with manual rollback steps and a checklist to identify affected BIOS images.

Next steps (action items):
- Coordinate with vendor to publish a BIOS microcode patch that removes redundant HID endpoints or provides compatibility flag (OOO: vendor ticket #DELL-2024-334).
- Implement udev coalescing rule in golden image and validate across fleet in staging region (assigned to Kernel/Platform team).
- Add automated detection to provisioning pipelines to flag images that cause >20 udev rate-limit events during first-boot (devops task).

Rollback plan: If vendor patch not available in 72 hours and depot throughput remains impacted, schedule a phased BIOS rollback for affected serial ranges (requires signed change controls).

Status: Mitigation in place; awaiting vendor patch. SLA extension recorded; manual triage procedure documented in Confluence.
